title: Interactive Cost Orienter: contextual walkthrough for Console cost dashboards and rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and prototype an in-product, stepwise walkthrough ("Orienter") that surfaces cost literacy and rollout impact before users take destructive actions. The Orienter should appear in empty or low-activity cost views and when a user is configuring a rollout that will materially change spend. Aim is to reduce surprise billing, educate developers about batching, KV cache benefits, and quantization trade-offs, and provide one-click remedial actions (estimate mode, simulated rollout).
problem_statement: Customers landing on the Console cost dashboards or initiating model rollouts often lack context for why costs spike and what conservative rollout settings look like. This leads to invoicing surprises and helpdesk tickets. Existing empty states are generic; we need contextual micro-education tied to the actual action the user is about to take.
goals: Reduce cost-related support tickets by educating users before rollout
Increase usage of conservative rollout presets (canary, traffic ramps) by 20%
Improve first-time cost dashboard comprehension for new accounts (survey-based)
user_personas: Product engineer: quickly launches experiments and needs safe defaults
Platform engineer: manages budgets for teams; needs repeatable rollout patterns
PM/Finance partner: wants clear explanations and quick links to billing insights
proposed_solution: An interactive, multi-step Orienter overlay that appears contextual to the page: A) On cost dashboard empty/low-traffic states show a lightweight explainer + sample workload presets, B) On rollout creation, show a simulated cost preview + recommended ramp plan, C) Offer in-line tooltips that explain batching, prefix caching, and quantization with links to quick deploy templates. Include an opt-in 'estimate mode' that runs a brief simulation against recent traffic to show expected token and GPU cost. Non-blocking, dismissible, and telemetry-instrumented.
user_testing_findings: (2026-02-26) 6 moderated sessions: users preferred a 3-step flow vs. a single long modal (3:1), citing cognitive load reduction
Participants asked for immediate 'what-if' sliders (traffic %, sequence length) — high signal to add simulate mode
Confusion observed around 'KV cache' term; rename and add micro-illustration and a link to docs
Prefer conservative default: users accepted '10% canary for 24h' in 5/6 sessions when given a recommended preset
accessibility_considerations: Ensure overlay is navigable by keyboard (tab order for steps, skip link to main content)
All interactive elements meet 4.5:1 color contrast; animations respect prefers-reduced-motion
Tooltips are reachable via focus and have aria-describedby attributes
design_decisions: Use a three-step microflow (Explain -> Simulate -> Apply) to reduce commitment friction
Keep Orienter non-modal on dashboards (inline panel) and modal on rollout creation for focused decision
Expose a lightweight simulated cost graph scaled to last 7-day baseline rather than absolute numbers to avoid legal exposure
Provide 3 recommended presets (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive) with default set to Conservative for new users
